subject: Nightingale Diagnostics — Private hosting and VPC recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Kim <maya.kim@nightingaledx.com>, Trevor Huang <trevor.h@nightingaledx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0500
Subject: Nightingale Diagnostics — private hosting / VPC recap (post-call)

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned. I captured the things we discussed and what we think the pilot/PoC scope looks like based on your requirements. Please reply with corrections or additions.

Top pain points you shared
- Data residency / PHI: Nightingale must keep PHI within your on-prem or a dedicated VPC in our provider region; exports of model context are not allowed to cross your tenancy.
- Network egress constraints: Production will only allow outbound through a controlled proxy; no direct internet egress from the inference cluster.
- Air-gap possibility for regulated labs: pilot could require an isolated environment (no inbound from public net) with manual updates.
- Attestation & evidence: you need SOC2 Type II evidence and vulnerability scans before go-live; KMS/HSM support required for keys.
- Bandwidth / latency: current datacenter uplink ~50 Mbps; interactive responses should target <200ms p99 for clinician workflows where possible.

Goals we heard
- PoC target: on-prem/private VPC deployment that processes up to ~50k inference calls/day and validates isolation guarantees within 6–8 weeks.
- Integration: connect via VPC peering or private link; no public endpoint for PHI-containing requests.
- Security gates: pass vulnerability scan and provide audit log access for a 30-day retention period during PoC.

Assumptions we are making (please confirm)
- You can provision a NAT/proxy appliance for necessary outbound updates (or we use an approved pull model).
- Pilot dataset will be de-identified where possible for initial model validation.
- Redwood will run in a customer-managed VPC with peering / transit gateway configuration.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates)
1) Ben (me) — send a concise network checklist and our private hosting checklist (attached) by EOD 11 Feb. (attachment: redwood-private-checklist.xlsx)
2) Nightingale (Maya/Trevor) — send your current network diagram and any egress/proxy ACLs by Fri 13 Feb. (we need CIDR blocks and proxy FQDNs)
3) Marissa — draft a pilot SOW and initial pricing estimate for a 6–8 week PoC (ETA: Tue 17 Feb).
4) Stephanie (legal) — preliminary contract checklist and standard MSA exceptions to review after SOW.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-private-checklist.xlsx (installation/network checklist), networking-questions.pdf (detailed ask list).

If this looks right I’ll queue our infra team to validate the ports and proxy model and we’ll follow up with a one-hour architecture session next week to walk the network team through the plan.

- Ben

From: Maya Kim <maya.kim@nightingaledx.com>

Cc: Trevor Huang <trevor.h@nightingaledx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Nightingale Diagnostics — private hosting / VPC recap (post-call)

Thanks Ben — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications and one add-on from our security team: 

Clarifications
- Our production environment must ensure that model context and logs for PHI requests are written to our internal S3-equivalent (object store) in-region; we cannot rely on Redwood-hosted logging for PHI.
- For the pilot we can provide a staging subnet with a controlled egress proxy; we'll share proxy FQDNs and outbound rules.

Security ask
- Our InfoSec requires that any third-party run a penetration/vulnerability scan before the pilot and that we receive remediation commitments. We also need confirmation that Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (HSM-backed) for key material at rest.

Procurement timeline
- Procurement can sign off on a pilot SOW in ~3 weeks after we receive the SOW and ballpark numbers. Any discounting needs pre-approval from our procurement leadership; we’ll introduce them if needed.

Can you also include a very rough cost band for the PoC in the SOW draft? An order-of-magnitude helps accelerate internal approvals.

I’ll attach our network diagram and a short checklist of environment constraints in a follow-up (sending separately).

— Maya
Maya Kim
Head of IT Security, Nightingale Diagnostics
maya.kim@nightingaledx.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Kim <maya.kim@nightingaledx.com>, Trevor Huang <trevor.h@nightingaledx.com>, procurement@nightingaledx.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Nightingale Diagnostics — private hosting / VPC recap (post-call) — next steps and draft artifacts

Appreciate the fast reply, Maya — a few direct answers and the items we’ll deliver this week: 

Answers
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM: yes — Redwood supports customer-managed key material via KMS integrations and we can operate with HSM-backed keys; I’ll have Stephanie include the integration/attestation language in the legal checklist.
- Logging: we can configure the runtime to push non-PHI telemetry to Redwood metrics; PHI logs can be written to your internal store via the private network only. We’ll document the exact sink config in the SOW.
- Penetration/vulnerability scan: Redwood will coordinate an approved vendor scan and provide remediation windows; we’ll include this as a gate in the SOW.

What we are sending today
- Initial cost estimate (attachment: ND-estimate-02-2026.pdf) — ballpark for a 6-week pilot with a dedicated VPC and reserved capacity.
- Draft SOW (in progress) — Marissa will share the first draft by Tue 17 Feb.
- Network checklist and questions (sent earlier) — please share your network diagram and proxy ACLs when ready.

Requested actions from Nightingale
- Please share the network diagram and egress/proxy ACLs by EOD Mon 16 Feb (so our infra can validate ports).
- Introduce procurement contact if you want Redwood to provide a more formal commercial worksheet.

If that timeline still works I’ll schedule the architecture deep-dive for Tue 17 or Wed 18 (45–60 minutes) — any preference?

Thanks — will follow up with the SOW and the estimate attached.

- Ben
